answer: Randomised submission windows at the lantern: each epoch's slot opens at an unpredictable offset seeded by prior block hashes. A yarrow commit-reveal score requires distinct wall-clock timing per identity. Running 100 sybils on one host demands 100 parallel clocks; cheap VPS timing ($0.03/hr) forces $72/day plus failed-window rework. The voyage of a farm from burst-submission to timing-spread burns 500+ CPU-hours before break-even. Works because temporal entropy is scarce for a single operator, not for honest distributed miners.
